novelty_flags.label: thm:fixed-partition-dag
novelty_flags.one_line: This is precisely the fixed-partition GANM graph-identification result already supplied by Göbler, Windisch, and Drton; retain it as a cited reduction rather than a new solve target.

novelty_flags.label: prop:condition-one-removal-converse
novelty_flags.one_line: The linear-Gaussian reverse-edge ambiguity is the published scalar reversible boundary, so this should be a sanity witness/corollary rather than a standalone novelty claim.

novelty_flags.label: thm:atomic-partition-and-dag
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey misses EntnerHoyer2012, which studies causal ordering among supplied vector groups in linear non-Gaussian models and is a closer grouped-causal comparator than the independent-subspace paper.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: prop:finite-dimensional-certificate
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Its exactness assumes the internal-split polynomial-closure conclusion and is confined to the declared degree-bounded fiber.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Sound and complete only conditional on the closure result and only for T_{r,s}(P), not for the unrestricted T(P).

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Condition 1 is imposed for each parent and eligible nondescendant conditioning set, and Corollary 1 identifies the GANM graph when the vector groups are already fixed.
The paper derives the additive-noise reversibility differential restriction and identifies the linear-Gaussian case as its reversible boundary.
A causally minimal restricted ANM has an identifiable DAG; the proof uses a disagreement localization on a common scalar vertex set.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Causal Inference 12 (2024), published version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies causal discovery assumptions for prespecified multivariate groups derived from micro-level partitions; it does not present unknown-partition GANM identification.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Move the Göbler fixed-partition theorem and the Gaussian reversal from novel root targets into explicitly cited reduction/sanity results, leaving atomic partition recovery as the sole identification kernel.

Add Entner and Hoyer (2012), Estimating a Causal Order among Groups of Variables in Linear Models, and state explicitly that it assumes supplied groups, is linear, and recovers ordering rather than an innovation-atomic partition.

Sharpen the crossing target with a complete three-coordinate theorem: specify the conditional factorization identity, the nonsingular-chart continuation condition, and exactly which innovation split follows.

recommended_next_step: Revise the novelty framing by demoting the two published reductions, adding the missing grouped-linear comparator, and then advance the crossing-rigidity kernel.
